scores.critique: Strongest solver spec (10 substeps, rest-length seam ramp, gravity ramp + 5x damping during sew, layer offsets, trilinear SDF with analytic gradient, v1 vertex-vertex self-collision, deterministic fixed step, primitive-mesh fallback before MarchingCubes) and the best body pipeline for a garment app: superellipse perimeter enforced by homogeneous scaling (correct), then re-measured with ray casts and shown as 'target vs actual' with a one-pass correction. Grading uses measurement-driven scaling plus per-vertex increments per size step (dx,dy)*(k-k_base), which is exactly a grade-rule table. But the garment semantics have real holes: (1) the sample 'front' has vertices spanning x=-240..240 AND mirrorAxis:'x' -- the doc's own half-piece convention contradicts its own fixture (either the piece is full and mirrorAxis must be null, or it must be x>=0 with the fold on x=0); (2) how a mirrorAxis piece is exported is unspecified -- offsetting the full mirrored outline would put seam allowance on the fold line; no 'PLACE ON FOLD' / 'Cut 1 on fold' label; (3) a single seamAllowanceMm per piece -- no per-edge allowance, so hem (25-40 mm), neckline (6 mm) and plain seams (10 mm) cannot coexist on one piece; (4) three unit conventions for the same quantity: body.params chest in cm but height in m, sizes.rows in mm, pattern in mm -- 'Fit body to size' and the Body panel are guaranteed conversion-bug surfaces; (5) T-shirt sample text says '6 seams' then lists 8; (6) index.html ids are only a naming convention (ctl-<panel>-<name>) and acceptance #10 refers to 'a fixed list' that is never given; (7) the geometry/ API (consumed by pattern, sizing, export, cloth) is named by file only, signatures are not in the frozen contract; (8) Bergou quadratic constraint written as C=1/2*coef*|L|^2: with alpha=0 a single projection only halves L (L_new = L/2) -- acceptable in PBD but the doc claims exactness; K-vector cot convention risk acknowledged; (9) arrangement blend formula uses an undefined 'right' vector; (10) 'tunneling impossible' holds only because 8.3 mm/substep < half the thinnest limb radius, not its diameter -- state it correctly; (11) popout runs a full duplicate sim, so A7 (UI shell + all panels + popout) is overloaded; (12) grid bake 580k cells x ~25 primitives is likely 300-500 ms not 150-300, the 30 mm drag grid mitigates. Acceptance suite is the most concrete (in-browser runAcceptance with numeric thresholds), checks 3/5/8/9 are directly automatable.

By far the most pattern-making-literate design: per-edge allowance with labels (hem 25 / neck 6 / fold 0), cutOnFold + fold edge, single/double notches, grainline, seam tool with live 'A 312 / B 328 -- ease 5.1%' readout and 8% warning, measure tool, grading with origin at CF (so the fold stays put) + per-point deltas interpolated by row index, seam-ease drift check per size, grade nest SVG, hem square-off at allowance discontinuities, notches reprojected onto the cut line, 100 mm calibration square on every tile, glue strips and crop marks, piece-measurements CSV with fabric consumption, shelf packer respecting grainline, 'closest size', 'Size from body', drape-any-size. SI units for body params and mm for chart are internally consistent. Technical errors: (1) torso section radii are solved with the Ramanujan ELLIPSE perimeter (closed form is correct: P is linear in a) but the section is rendered/collided as a SUPERELLIPSE with e=2.0-2.4 whose perimeter is larger -- acceptance #5 'measure within 0.5%' cannot pass as written; (2) stretch compliance 'scaled by 1/edgeLength for resolution independence' is backwards for a 2D membrane (lattice edge stiffness ~ Y is already length-independent; the 1/L scaling makes cotton ~67x softer than the table implies); (3) no self-collision in v1 -- for a SIGGRAPH-style demo front/back and layered garments will interpenetrate; (4) analytic min-union SDF with finite-difference normals: pow() with fractional exponent + binary search + 3-tap FD per particle per substep (6000x8) is realistically 5-10 ms, not '<2 ms'; FD normals across the min-union are discontinuous (jitter at armpit/crotch), and there is no smooth blend; (5) superellipse 'pseudo-distance' underestimates real distance by up to 30% where rx != rz; (6) measure by slicing a render mesh that is a concatenation of overlapping primitives yields multiple loops (arms) -- must slice the analytic loft only; (7) T-shirt sample text '5 seams ... = 8 seams' is self-contradictory; (8) 'zip' modelled as a compliant seam is semantically wrong (a zip is a closure); (9) src/app ownership 'U or lead' is ambiguous and U also owns all panels + session + debugApi wiring; X (export) is hard-blocked on P's offset/grading; (10) segments store redundant p0/p1 endpoints with an invariant to maintain -- extra conflict surface for E and P; (11) acceptance #12 (popout window title + topology message) needs cross-window automation; #11 'byte-identical JSON' needs guaranteed key order. Displacement clamp 5 cm/substep is larger than a forearm radius (velocity clamp saves it).

Cleanest ownership (A0 lead + 9 agents, one directory each, enumerated element ids, init(ctx) per module, docs/CONTRACTS.md, consumer-adapts rule) and the most automation-friendly API (ready promise, sim.step(n) returns stats synchronously, ui.click(id), getMeshStats). Mesher is well reasoned: Gabriel-condition argument for boundary preservation, notch t values forced to mesh vertices, midpoint insertion mirrored onto the seam partner to keep pairing, seam CHAINS over multiple edges with proportional arc-length pairing, edge-renumbering index map on split, Laplacian smoothing with flip rejection. Errors: (1) bending compliances are 50-500x too stiff: at h_sub=1/360 s and w~3.4e4 per vertex, cotton bend 4e-4 gives alpha~/(sum w|grad C|^2) ~ 8e-4 -- effectively rigid; even chiffon (8e-3) comes out stiffer than a sensible denim, so every fabric drapes like cardboard and no acceptance check would catch it; jersey stretch 4e-5 also does not stretch; (2) Ramanujan solved by 'bisection, 5 iterations, <0.1%' is wrong -- 5 bisections on a plausible bracket leave ~1 cm error; P is linear in a, use the closed form; (3) sample front is a 300x650 mm full rectangle with quantity 1 for a 92 cm chest body -- front+back = 600 mm < 920 mm, the fixture cannot fit the default body; (4) no cut-on-fold concept ('symmetry' is only an editing aid), single seamAllowance_mm per piece, no double notches, no calibration square on the print tiles (only a page label) -- weak on export correctness; (5) offset loop removal tests only the next 30 segments at 0.5 mm chords, but a loop at a 60-degree concave corner with 10 mm SA spans ~70 segments -- loops will survive on necklines/armholes; (6) acceptance #9 tile count ceil(W/190)*ceil(H/277) ignores the 10 mm overlap the same section specifies (step must be 180x267); (7) acceptance #13 clicks the canvas 'at known mm->px coordinates' but no mm->px mapping is exposed on __app; (8) pattern space y-DOWN with 'CCW' outlines and 'right-hand normal for CCW' -- orientation sign must be pinned in geometry.js or A2/A3/A7 will disagree; (9) fabric/ presets (a contract consumed by physics and render3d) are owned by the UI agent A8, and core/geometry.js lives in the frozen contracts dir but is written by A1 -- both are late-arriving dependencies for three agents; (10) adaptive substep drop (10->4 under load) breaks determinism for automation; vMax 8 m/s is high; (11) SDF gradient by central differences of trilinear samples (6 extra samples) instead of the analytic trilinear derivative; grid bake 0.94 M cells x 17 primitives is likely 300-500 ms not 150 (debounce + old-grid-until-swap mitigates); (12) grading is proportional only (length by height gives a 5.7% length grade per 10 cm height, larger than industry length grades), no per-point rules.

grafts: From patternmaking-first: per-EDGE seam allowance with edge labels (hem 25, neck 6, plain 10, fold 0) instead of one seamAllowanceMm per piece; offset must handle allowance discontinuities with the hem square-off rule and reproject notches onto the cut line.

From patternmaking-first: explicit cutOnFold + fold edge semantics: half-piece stored with x>=0, mirrored only at mesh time, exported as the half with a dash-dot fold line, 'PLACE ON FOLD' and 'CUT 1 ON FOLD' in the label block, zero allowance on the fold edge.

From patternmaking-first: seam tool status readout 'A 312 mm / B 328 mm -- ease 5.1%' and a __app.pattern.seamEase(id) query; single/double notches; measure tool; validate() returning [{level,msg,pieceId}].
From patternmaking-first: 100 mm calibration square on EVERY print tile plus crop marks, glue strips and tile labels; 'Scale 100%, no fit-to-page' header on the print page.

From patternmaking-first: grade nest SVG (all sizes per piece, colour per size), piece-measurements CSV per size (edge lengths, seam ease %, area, fabric consumption from the packer), 'closest size' readout in the Body panel, 'Size from body' row creation, and 'drape any size' (graded pieces + body fitted to that row).
From patternmaking-first: Fabric as a project-level entity {id, preset, color, pattern, overrides} referenced by pieces (fabric A/B), rather than fabricId+color duplicated on every piece.
From patternmaking-first: ear-clipping + midpoint subdivision as a last-resort mesher fallback so a piece never fails to mesh; per-particle NaN restore from xPrev before escalating to a full reset.

From product-first: seams over CHAINS of consecutive edges ({piece, edges:[...]}) with proportional arc-length pairing and chain corners forced as samples; notch t values forced to boundary mesh vertices; midpoint insertion during boundary repair mirrored onto the seam partner at the same fraction so pairing never breaks.
From product-first: edge-renumbering index map emitted on split/insert so seams and notches referencing later edges are shifted inside the editor before commit.
From product-first: cheap CCD -- if the SDF sign flips between xPrev and x, project to the surface on xPrev's side; keep colliding with the old SDF grid until the new bake is swapped in (debounced).

From product-first: automation ergonomics -- __app.ready promise, sim.step(n) returns SimStats synchronously with rendering suppressed, ui.click(id), a fully enumerated id list in index.html written in Phase 0 (not just a naming convention), and a __app.pattern.mmToPx/pxToMm helper for canvas-driving tests.

From product-first: Laplacian smoothing of interior mesh vertices with triangle-flip rejection; mesher auto-raises h to keep the vertex cap; 'reduced quality' status when over budget (but only when not in step(n) mode).
corrections: physics-first sample fixture contradicts its own mirror convention: 'front' has vertices at x=-240..240 AND mirrorAxis:'x'. Pick one rule (half piece with x>=0, fold on x=0) and make the sample obey it; never offset the fold edge when exporting the half.

physics-first mixes three unit conventions for body measurements (params chest in cm, height in m, size-chart rows in mm). Use one unit for the whole document (mm, or cm with explicit _cm suffixes as product-first does) and convert only at the UI boundary and at the mm->m step into the solver.

patternmaking-first solves section radii with the Ramanujan ELLIPSE perimeter but renders/collides a SUPERELLIPSE (e=2.0-2.4); the chest measurement will overshoot by several % and acceptance 'within 0.5%' fails. Compute the superellipse perimeter numerically (P is homogeneous degree 1, so scale linearly as physics-first does) or use true ellipses.

patternmaking-first's 'stretch compliance scaled by 1/edgeLength for resolution independence' is wrong for a 2D membrane (lattice edge stiffness ~ Y, already length-independent). Do not scale distance compliance by 1/L; if anything scale BEND compliance by (h/h_ref)^2.

product-first bending compliances are 50-500x too stiff: with h_sub=1/360 s and w~3.4e4 per vertex, alpha_bend=4e-4 gives alpha~/(sum w|gradC|^2)~1e-3 (rigid). Tune every fabric by the dimensionless ratio alpha/(h_sub^2 * sum w|gradC|^2) -- target ~0.05 (denim/leather) to ~5 (chiffon) -- and add a drape-sag acceptance check (30x30 cm sheet pinned at two corners: sag > X cm for cotton, > Y for silk) so a cardboard result cannot pass.
product-first 'Ramanujan by bisection, 5 iterations, <0.1%' is false (5 bisections leave ~1 cm on a plausible bracket). P is linear in a: a = C / (pi*[3(1+k) - sqrt((3+k)(1+3k))]).

product-first offset loop removal only scans the next 30 segments at 0.5 mm chords; a loop at a sharp concave corner with 10 mm SA spans ~70 segments. Use a full O(n^2) segment-pair scan (n<=~4000 is fine) or sample the stitch polyline at 2 mm before offsetting.
product-first acceptance tile count ceil(W/190)*ceil(H/277) ignores the 10 mm overlap it specifies; the tile step is (window - overlap) = 180x267. physics-first must also state the step explicitly.

product-first sample T-shirt (300x650 mm full front, quantity 1) cannot fit a 92 cm chest (front+back 600 mm < 920 mm). Sample garments must be authored to body + ease (each panel >= half chest/2 + 15-30 mm ease) and Phase 0 must verify seam-partner lengths with the mesher.

Both physics-first ('6 seams' then 8 listed) and patternmaking-first ('5 seams ... = 8') miscount the T-shirt seams. A set-in-sleeve tee has 8: 2 shoulder, 2 side, 2 sleeve underarm, 2 sleeve cap/armhole.

physics-first quadratic bending C = 1/2*coef*|L|^2: with alpha=0 a single projection only halves L (Delta-lambda is constant in |L|), and the constraint is quadratic so the compliance table is not in m/N. Either drop the 1/2 (full projection per substep), or use the linear form C=|L|*sqrt(coef); add the flat-patch C=0 / bent-patch C>0 unit test in either case.

patternmaking-first: analytic min-union SDF with finite-difference normals gives discontinuous normals at armpit/crotch and the pow()-based loft costs far more than '<2 ms'; if analytic SDFs are kept, use analytic gradients, a polynomial smooth-min at joints, and a bake-to-grid path as fallback (physics-first's 15 mm grid + analytic trilinear gradient is the safer default).
patternmaking-first measure.js must slice the analytic torso loft, not the concatenated render mesh (arms produce extra loops at chest height); physics-first's ray limit 1.5*a handles this.

product-first: pin the outline orientation sign in core/geometry.js (polygonArea sign in the y-down space) and make offset/mesher/export all use it; do not describe 'CCW' without stating the axis convention.
product-first: adaptive substep reduction must be disabled inside sim.step(n)/automation, otherwise acceptance numbers are non-deterministic; keep a fixed dt as physics-first specifies.

physics-first: the 'tunneling impossible' argument must compare per-substep displacement with the limb RADIUS (wrist ~25 mm), not thickness; 8.3 mm still passes but state it correctly and keep the displacement clamp.

physics-first: enumerate the geometry/ API signatures (sampleByArcLength, lengthOf, offsetPolygon, remesh, pack, pointInPolygon, distToPolyline) in the frozen contract, since three agents consume it; move fabric presets (product-first) and geometry (product-first) out of UI/A1 ownership into Phase 0.

All three: define the export convention for mirrored/on-fold pieces before agents fan out (half with fold label vs full piece), and ensure notch ticks are perpendicular to the CUT line and span stitch->cut; sizes CSV should default to cm (industry) while the document stores mm.
